sections.h2: Which office in Rutherfordton files Rutherford County deeds?
sections.html:
The Rutherford County Register of Deeds works from 229 North Main Street in Rutherfordton. Postal mail goes to Post Office Box 551, Rutherfordton, NC 28139. According to the county site, the doors are open 8:30 to 5:00 on weekdays, minus holiday closures.

Two phone lines are published: 828-287-6155 for the main desk and 828-287-6195 for the record room. The county says its holdings reach back into the 1700s, which is useful context for anyone selling a family tract that has passed through many hands in the foothills.

Most sellers never walk in. A closing attorney or title company sends the deed over. Knowing the office's rules still pays off, since a rejected deed pushes back your closing and your payout.

sections.h2: What papers does Rutherford County keep besides deeds?
sections.html:
The county lists a wide range of public records in its Rutherford register collection:

  • Real estate conveyances and deeds of trust, with their cancellations
  • Assumed names and powers of attorney
  • Road maintenance agreements and plats
  • Separation agreements and similar filings

An online index lets you search by name. A separate alert tool named Property Check emails you when something new is filed against a name or parcel you choose. An owner of a vacant or inherited house can use it to catch an unexpected lien or a forged transfer early.

sections.h2: How must a deed be formatted for the Rutherford County clerk?
sections.html:
Under G.S. 161-14, the county lists layout rules that a deed must meet on the page. Check each one against your draft:

  • A deed or deed of trust names its preparer on page one.
  • The sheet measures either 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Page one leaves three blank inches at the top, and all other edges keep at least a half inch free.
  • Black text on white paper, in type no smaller than 9 points, printed on a single side.
  • The title of the instrument appears at the top of the first page.

Pen is allowed for filling blanks and for corrections. A pre-signing review by your attorney is the cheapest way to avoid a bounced filing.

sections.h2: Will late property tax stop a Rutherford County deed from recording?
sections.html:
It will. The register of deeds says G.S. 161-10(a)(19), in force since October 1, 2011, requires delinquent taxes to be paid before a deed is recorded.

The reason is the lien. State law attaches the county tax lien to the parcel as of the listing date, with penalties, interest and costs added on (G.S. 105-355). Left unpaid, the debt can end in an auction on the courthouse steps, and anyone redeeming ahead of confirmation owes the taxes along with penalties, interest and costs (G.S. 105-374).

Ask the Rutherford County tax collector for a written balance on each parcel before you accept an offer. Your closing attorney can then settle it from the proceeds.

sections.h2: What fees does the Rutherford County recorder collect?
sections.html:
Charges come from G.S. 161-10 and apply statewide. The county adds that military discharges are recorded free and that no charge applies to filing a deed of trust satisfaction.

Fees at the Rutherford County recording desk
ItemPrinted figureSource
General instrument, first 15 pages$26.00 (add $4.00 per extra page)G.S. 161-10
Deed of trust, first 35 pages$64.00 (add $4.00 per extra page)G.S. 161-10
Deed of trust satisfactionNoneCounty page
Military dischargeNoneCounty page
Plat sheet$21.00G.S. 161-10

The statute calls the schedule complete and exclusive, and the fee is paid before filing.

sections.h2: What does the seller owe in deed excise tax in Rutherford County?
sections.html:
The seller pays, at a rate of $1.00 per $500 of price or value (or part of $500), handed over before the deed is recorded (G.S. 105-228.30). Half of the money stays with the county and half goes to the state.

A cash sale is a conveyance for value, so the tax applies. Ask your attorney to print it on its own line of the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Does Rutherford County accept electronic filing?
sections.html:
Yes. The county notes that e-recording through Simplifile began in the office on April 24, 2018, with plats added on February 1, 2022. It also states that microfilming began January 1, 2017.

Speed matters because registration time sets rank. A deed or long lease binds lien creditors and later purchasers for value only from the moment it is registered, and the earlier filing wins (G.S. 47-18). When a buyer's lender and a seller's lender both file on closing day, a same-day electronic filing keeps your deal clean.

Anyone unsure about a particular document can call the main desk at 828-287-6155 before sending it.

faqs.q: What days is the Rutherford County recorder open?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:30 to 5:00, with holiday closures, per the county site. The main line is 828-287-6155. Calling first avoids a wasted trip on a holiday week.

faqs.q: Is filing a deed of trust satisfaction free in Rutherford County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county page says no charge applies to satisfactions, and state law agrees. Make sure your lender files one after payoff.

faqs.q: Who covers the transfer tax on a house sale in Rutherford County?
faqs.a: The seller covers it. The rate is $1.00 per $500 of value under G.S. 105-228.30, paid before recording. It should appear as a separate settlement line.

faqs.q: Can overdue taxes hold up my Rutherford County deed?
faqs.a: They can. The register of deeds says delinquent taxes must be paid first under G.S. 161-10(a)(19). Get a balance from the tax collector and settle it at closing.

faqs.q: Does Rutherford County take electronic recordings?
faqs.a: Yes. E-recording via Simplifile started April 24, 2018, and plat e-recording started February 1, 2022. Title companies and attorneys generally use it.
